findingDetails.title: Over-limit dispatch commands bypass Pi authorization
findingDetails.evidence: inspectDispatch returns kind none for any command longer than 32768 characters; Pi preflight returns on kind none before shouldDenyPiDispatch.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The shared inspector is the matcher used by the Pi tool_call path; a padded direct command was probed and returned kind none.
findingDetails.recommendation: Classify over-limit dispatch-shaped input as ambiguous or fail closed, and add a padded direct-dispatch regression.
findingDetails.claim: A caller can bypass the Pi default-dispatch policy by making a direct external dispatch exceed MAX_INSPECTED_COMMAND_CHARS.
evidenceRefs: probe: padded devin command -> kind none
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A lower upstream Pi/shell limit or a second preflight rejecting over-limit dispatch candidates.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The bound may be intended only as a resource guard, but the reviewed Pi path has no second classifier.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: An upstream limit or second guard proves the command cannot reach execution.

findingDetails.title: Unquoted echo text is treated as an ambiguous dispatch and blocked
findingDetails.evidence: hasDispatchEvidence requires only an unquoted executor token and print flag, not executable position; echo devin -p task becomes ambiguous and Pi blocks every ambiguous inspection.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The predicate is command-head agnostic; existing negative coverage uses quoted echo only.
findingDetails.recommendation: Require executable-position evidence or model safe echo/printf heads; add unquoted negative controls.
findingDetails.claim: A harmless command that prints the words devin -p task is blocked as an external dispatch.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A documented policy intentionally blocking unquoted echo/printf text or a parser rule filtering safe text emitters.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The parser may conservatively block opaque syntax, but the packet explicitly lists echo/printf text as non-dispatch controls.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: The contract is narrowed to permit this false positive.

findingDetails.title: Write containment exempts pre-existing dirty paths by name only
findingDetails.evidence: The baseline stores only path strings; detection skips any current out-of-scope path in preSet without comparing status/content. A leaf can modify an already-dirty file or delete a pre-existing untracked file without a new violation.
findingDetails.scopeProof: snapshotOutOfScopeDirtyPaths and detectNewOutOfScopeViolations are the complete baseline/diff pair; no content or presence comparison appears.
findingDetails.recommendation: Capture content/presence or another immutable baseline and detect changes separately from unchanged dirty paths.
findingDetails.claim: The structural write-containment guard does not detect mutations to pre-existing out-of-scope dirty paths.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Caller-level content snapshots or a guarantee that guarded leaves cannot touch pre-existing dirty paths.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Path-only subtraction may avoid reverting operator work, but it does not prove that work was unchanged.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: An external baseline or read-only guarantee is proven.

findingDetails.title: Receipt paths accept traversal-capable caller input
findingDetails.evidence: receiptPaths joins caller-supplied receiptDir and dispatchId without validating either value; beginReceipt passes dispatchId directly and writeReceiptAtomic creates and renames the result.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The input-to-write path is executor-audit.ts:146-151, 515-519, 531-537, and 605-614; no safe-identifier allowlist or resolved-path descendant check appears.
findingDetails.recommendation: Restrict dispatchId to a path-safe identifier and verify resolved receipt paths remain descendants of a trusted receiptDir.
findingDetails.claim: Malformed receiptDir or dispatchId input can redirect intent/completion writes outside the intended parent-owned receipt directory.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Every production caller uses a fixed trusted receiptDir and generated-only dispatchId, with no external configuration able to supply path components.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The API may be intended as an internal seam, but it accepts both values as ordinary input and does not enforce that trust boundary.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A complete caller audit proves only sanitized generated identifiers reach the writer and rejects caller-supplied path components.

findingDetails.title: Non-Codex fanout leaves run write-capable without structural containment
findingDetails.evidence: The runner selects a write-capable sandbox and documents a prompt-only lineageDir boundary, but enables structural containment only when lineage.kind is cli-codex. Other fanout executors have no post-dispatch diff/revert guard in this path.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The write-capable default is at fanout-run.cjs:2261-2267; the sole containment condition is at 2366 and guard invocation is conditional at 2424-2457.
findingDetails.recommendation: Enforce a real filesystem boundary for every writable executor or fail closed before dispatch when no boundary exists.
findingDetails.claim: A non-Codex fanout worker can write outside its lineageDir without runtime detection or reversion.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Each non-Codex adapter enforces a filesystem boundary independently, or the contract explicitly permits arbitrary repository writes for those executor kinds.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Some provider CLIs may enforce their own sandbox, but the reviewed runner does not establish that for every non-Codex kind and deliberately chooses a write-capable mode.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Adapter-specific enforcement or a verified read-only mode is proven for every non-Codex lineage kind reachable by fanout.

findingDetails.title: Pi nonzero exits are accepted when partial artifacts remain
findingDetails.evidence: Every nonzero cli-pi exit is exempted from the failure branch, and the remaining gate checks only expected-artifact presence. A process can leave partial files, exit nonzero, and still be returned as fulfilled.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The cli-pi exception is at fanout-run.cjs:2481-2487; artifact presence is checked at 2502-2512; no terminal-success invariant is checked.
findingDetails.recommendation: Require a terminal-success record or a narrowly defined benign exit contract tied to complete artifacts.
findingDetails.claim: A failed Pi dispatch can be recorded as successful if it leaves enough partial artifacts for presence checks to pass.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The Pi adapter guarantees every nonzero exit occurs only after a complete terminal artifact set, with a regression test for failure after artifact creation.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Observed nondeterministic Pi nonzero exits may be benign, but that does not prove all such exits are harmless or that artifact presence proves completion.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A provider contract and integration test bind benign nonzero exits to an exact durable terminal-success marker.
